headline: Rates are the dominant driver: 10Y near multi-decade highs after a September Fed hike, equities still near records, crypto data thin
tldr: Research was degraded this run (Hyperliquid API and most live quote feeds unreachable; web-search figures partly conflicting), so levels below are low-confidence. Macro: the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 and an Oct 27-28 follow-up is roughly a coin-flip per prediction markets; the 10Y sits around 5.3%, the highest since 2002. Equities: S&P 500 about 7,770-7,810, near a record, led by AI-linked earnings. Crypto: ETH about $2.7K, BTC reported anywhere from the high $60Ks to mid-$80Ks depending on source. Geopolitics: a new Russia/Iran sanctions law carries an Oct 18 implementation deadline with possible tariffs on large importers of Russian energy. Watch: Oct 18 sanctions deadline, September CPI, Oct 27-28 FOMC. Not financial advice.

domains.summary: Policy is tightening: the FOMC raised the target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 (first hike since 2023) and 16 of 18 participants projected at least one more hike this year. Long yields spiked on Oct 5 (10Y about 5.34%, 30Y about 5.70%, highest since 2002) and eased slightly on Oct 6 (10Y about 5.27%). We read the liquidity backdrop as tightening. No September CPI print or current oil/dollar levels could be verified this run.

US cash market status at write time unknown; levels are as of the Oct 5-6 sessions. Indexes are near record highs despite the rates spike, with AI-linked names accounting for the bulk of 2026 index gains per Jefferies. Volatility was subdued at the last verified reading (VIX 15.31 on Oct 2). No put/call or Oct 7 close found.

Hyperliquid metaAndAssetCtxs was unreachable from this environment, so perp OI and funding are not reported (last public milestone: platform OI record about $18B on Sep 23, two-sided). Spot: ETH about $2,725 as of Oct 5; BTC reported near $84.8K on Oct 4 by one note, though a market-cap figure in another source implies a much lower price, so treat BTC as low-confidence. Sentiment readings could not be dated.

Individual mega-cap quotes for Oct 6-7 could not be found this run, so dispersion is not assessed. Context: AI-linked stocks drove more than 80% of S&P 500 gains in 2026 per Jefferies, hyperscaler 2026 capex estimates run $520-725B depending on scope, and NVDA is about 22% of SMH, keeping semis breadth concentrated. Oct 2 coverage described semis as split.

The Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (signed Sep 18) requires implementation within 30 days (Oct 18), with authority for tariffs up to 100% on top importers of Russian energy, subject to waivers. Separately reported: US-Canada 50% tariffs after talks broke down (undated roundup), prospective new China overcapacity tariffs, new Iran-related Treasury sanctions, and an Iran-Oman Hormuz transit framework. Current Brent/WTI and OPEC+ news not found.

thesis.observe: The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 with most participants projecting more. The 10Y reached about 5.34% on Oct 5, the highest since 2002, then about 5.27% on Oct 6. The S&P 500 is around 7,770-7,810, near its Aug 13 record close. VIX was 15.31 on Oct 2. ETH was about $2,725 on Oct 5. A Russia/Iran sanctions law has an Oct 18 implementation deadline. Hyperliquid data, September CPI, oil and mega-cap quotes were not retrievable.
thesis.infer: Equities appear to be pricing earnings growth in AI-linked names as outweighing a sharp rise in long-end yields; we read that as a setup sensitive to any further long-yield move. Consensus is pricing roughly even odds of an October hike; the data gap (no September CPI) limits how far we can diverge from that. Crypto reads as range-bound and idiosyncratic, but source conflicts on BTC mean this is a low-confidence read.
thesis.forecast: Base case (we lean here, low-confidence given degraded data): range-bound equities near highs while long yields stay elevated and the October FOMC odds drift with incoming data. Tail case (low-confidence): a further long-end yield spike or a hot inflation print forces a repricing of hike odds and a volatility jump, with risk skews toward long-duration tech. A second tail case (low-confidence): tariff implementation under the Oct 18 sanctions deadline broadens into a trade shock. Consensus is pricing a split decision in October; we read the risk as dependent on September CPI, which we could not verify.
thesis.disclaimer: Not financial advice. Market intelligence only — a reasoned read of public data, not a recommendation to buy or sell anything.

risks: Further long-end yield spike (30Y already above 5.7%) pressuring valuations
Hawkish surprise at the Oct 27-28 FOMC or hot September CPI
Tariff escalation tied to the Oct 18 Russia/Iran sanctions deadline or US-Canada/China trade measures
Data-quality risk: this run lacked Hyperliquid and several live quote feeds, so levels may be stale
